models._description: Adds oauth_provider_id, oauth_uid, oauth_access_token (NO_ACCESS), has_oauth_access_token + OAuth auth hooks
Adds auth_oauth_google_enabled / auth_oauth_google_client_id / server_uri_google (Google quick-config bridge to provider_google)
init() seeds provider_openerp.client_id from database.uuid on force install

behavioral_notes.observation: auth.oauth.provider is a small config model that stores one external identity provider's OAuth2 wiring: client_id (our app registration at the IdP), auth_endpoint (required Authorization URL the browser is redirected to), scope (default 'openid profile email'), validation_endpoint (required UserInfo/tokeninfo URL), data_endpoint (optional extra profile fetch), plus presentation fields enabled/css_class/body (the translatable login-button label) and sequence (_order='sequence, name'). Seed data/auth_oauth_data.xml ships three ready providers — provider_openerp (Odoo.com Accounts, accounts.odoo.com/oauth2), provider_google (Google OAuth2, accounts.google.com) and provider_facebook (Facebook Graph, with a data_endpoint for id,name,email) — but none is enabled by default; an admin must set enabled and supply a client_id. ir.config_parameter.init(force=True) backfills provider_openerp.client_id from database.uuid so the Odoo Account provider self-identifies. res.config.settings exposes only Google as a one-click Settings toggle (set_values writes back to provider_google). Only base.group_system may read/write providers (single ACL access_auth_oauth_provider).

behavioral_notes.element: controllers/main.py OAuthLogin.list_providers / web_login (login-page button injection + state CSRF)
behavioral_notes.observation: OAuthLogin subclasses auth_signup's Home and overrides web_login: it loads every enabled provider via sudo().search_read and, for each, builds an auth_link = 'auth_endpoint?response_type=token&client_id=..&redirect_uri={url_root}auth_oauth/signin&scope=..&state={json}'. The implicit 'token' flow returns the access token in the URL fragment. get_state packs the opaque state dict d=session.db, p=provider.id, r=url_quote(redirect target) and optionally t=signup token; this state is the CSRF/round-trip binding — on return /auth_oauth/signin trusts it to recover db, provider and post-login redirect, and refuses (BadRequest) if state['d'] is not in db_filter. The providers list is pushed into the QWeb login template's qcontext (template 'providers' inherits web.login_oauth) so the 'Sign in with Google/Odoo.com/...' buttons render on the standard login form; oauth_error query param (1/2/3) is mapped to a human message shown on the page.

behavioral_notes.element: /auth_oauth/signin controller + res.users.auth_oauth -> _auth_oauth_validate (token verification against the IdP)
behavioral_notes.observation: The OAuth callback. The IdP redirects back to /auth_oauth/signin with the access_token in the URL fragment; @fragment_to_query_string rewrites the fragment into query args so the server can read it. The controller json.loads(state), re-resolves the db via ensure_db, then calls res.users.with_user(SUPERUSER_ID).auth_oauth(provider, kw). auth_oauth -> _auth_oauth_validate makes a server-to-server requests.get to the provider's validation_endpoint (Bearer header or access_token param, controlled by the auth_oauth.authorization_header ICP, 10s timeout) and, if data_endpoint is set, a second GET merged in; it then unifies the subject identity by popping 'sub' (standard), then 'id' (google v1/facebook), then 'user_id' (google tokeninfo/odoo) and raises AccessDenied('Missing subject identity') if none. This is the trust pivot: the access token is validated with the IdP, not just decoded locally. A code comment flags the Confused-Deputy/audience-check caveat (validation.audience vs OUR client_id) as intentionally not enforced here.

_auth_oauth_signin matches the validated subject to a local account by search([('oauth_uid','=',uid),('oauth_provider_id','=',provider)]) — the unique(oauth_provider_id, oauth_uid) constraint guarantees at most one. On match it writes the fresh oauth_access_token and returns the login. On no match (AccessDenied) it provisions a NEW user via self.signup(values, token) using _generate_signup_values: login/email come from validation['email'] (falling back to a synthetic 'provider_{p}_user_{uid}'), name from validation['name'], wiring oauth_provider_id/oauth_uid/oauth_access_token and active=True — i.e. just-in-time account creation governed by auth_signup's signup mode (the t= state token carries an invitation). If no_user_creation context is set (the /auth_oauth/oea Odoo-Account path uses it) signup is skipped and None is returned. Back in the controller, request.env.cr.commit() makes the new user visible before session.authenticate runs a separate transaction; the session is then established with credential type 'oauth_token'.

OAuth extends the credential pipeline: _check_credentials first delegates to super (password/apikey) and only on AccessDenied tries the OAuth branch — it accepts when credential['type']=='oauth_token' and a sudo search finds the current uid holding that exact oauth_access_token, returning auth_method='oauth', mfa='default'. The stored token is gated: oauth_access_token is groups=fields.NO_ACCESS, prefetch=False, readonly; only has_oauth_access_token (a computed bool, group_erp_manager) is exposed, and SELF_READABLE_FIELDS is widened to include it. remove_oauth_access_token lets the user or an ERP manager clear the token (logout of the federation). oauth_access_token is added to _get_session_token_fields, so changing/clearing it invalidates the session token — a credential rotation logs the federated session out. Password-RPC interplay: the OAuth branch is only allowed when interactive or the user is not _rpc_api_keys_only.

No OWL components, JS modules, registry adds, services or patches. The only client footprint is static/src/scss/auth_oauth.scss (provider-button icon styling — .o_auth_oauth_provider_icon and per-provider .o_google_provider/.o_facebook_provider/.o_odoo_provider classes referenced from the provider css_class field) loaded into the web.assets_frontend bundle, plus the server-rendered QWeb template 'providers' (views/auth_oauth_templates.xml) which inherits web.login_oauth to t-foreach the enabled providers into login buttons. The whole 'Log in with Google/Azure/etc.' UI is server-rendered onto the standard login page, not a custom OWL widget.

behavioral_notes.element: external Identity Provider integration (gap #7: outbound OAuth2 calls)
behavioral_notes.observation: auth_oauth is fundamentally an outbound-integration module: it imports the requests SDK and makes 2 server-to-server HTTP call sites in models/res_users.py._auth_oauth_rpc (GET validation_endpoint, GET data_endpoint) to external identity providers — Google (accounts.google.com / googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/userinfo), Facebook Graph (graph.facebook.com/me) and Odoo.com Accounts (accounts.odoo.com/oauth2/tokeninfo) shipped as seed data, plus any custom OIDC/OAuth2 IdP (Azure AD/Entra, Okta, etc.) configured by the admin. The browser-side leg (auth_endpoint redirect, token-in-fragment) is the implicit OAuth2 flow; uses_api_keys=true reflects the per-provider client_id app credential. Endpoints are admin-configured rather than hardcoded, so extract_frontend reports endpoints=[]; the real targets live in the auth.oauth.provider records.

it_architecture.application: auth_oauth (OAuth2 single-sign-on: federated 'Log in with Google/Facebook/Odoo.com/Azure/Okta' external-identity login layered on the web/auth_signup login flow)
software_services: /auth_oauth/signin (public HTTP: OAuth2 callback; fragment->query, token validation, signin/signup, session establish)
/auth_oauth/oea (public HTTP: Odoo.com Account login shortcut, no_user_creation)
/web/login (override: inject enabled-provider buttons + oauth_error messaging into the login page)
logical_data_erm: res.users -N::1-> auth.oauth.provider (oauth_provider_id; which IdP federated this account)
res.users.(oauth_provider_id, oauth_uid) UNIQUE (one external identity == one local user per provider)
information_flows: depends: base, web, base_setup, auth_signup (extends web's login controller + reuses auth_signup just-in-time user creation)
login-redirect: web_login -> list_providers -> auth_link (auth_endpoint?client_id&redirect_uri&scope&state) -> browser to external IdP
callback: IdP -> /auth_oauth/signin (token in fragment) -> auth_oauth -> _auth_oauth_validate -> requests.get(validation_endpoint[/data_endpoint]) at external IdP
match/provision: _auth_oauth_signin -> search by (oauth_uid, provider) -> existing login | _generate_signup_values -> auth_signup.signup (new res.users)
session: cr.commit() -> session.authenticate(credential type=oauth_token) -> _check_credentials(oauth_token) -> session finalize / redirect
side-effect: oauth_access_token in _get_session_token_fields -> rotating/removing the token invalidates the session
config: res.config.settings.set_values -> auth_oauth.provider_google.write(enabled, client_id); ir.config_parameter.init(force) -> provider_openerp.client_id

capabilities: Identity Provider Configuration & Onboarding (per-IdP endpoints, client_id, scope)
OAuth2 Access-Token Validation against the provider (UserInfo/tokeninfo)
Just-in-Time Account Provisioning on First SSO Login (via auth_signup)
value_streams: Configure-Provider: admin enables an IdP -> sets client_id/endpoints/scope -> 'Sign in with X' button appears on the login page
SSO-Login-to-Session: click provider -> IdP redirect/consent -> token callback -> validate token -> match or provision res.users -> finalized authenticated session
information_concepts: OAuth state token (CSRF/round-trip binding: db, provider, redirect, signup token)
policies: Single ACL: only base.group_system may read/write auth.oauth.provider (no record rules)
Identity-uniqueness policy: unique(oauth_provider_id, oauth_uid) — one external identity maps to exactly one local user per provider
Trust policy: an access token must be validated server-to-server against the provider's validation_endpoint before any session is granted; missing subject -> AccessDenied
Provisioning policy: new-user creation on SSO is gated by auth_signup signup mode + the state token; no_user_creation (Odoo-Account path) blocks it

Token-as-session policy: oauth_access_token is groups=NO_ACCESS and part of the session-token fields, so clearing/rotating it logs the federated session out; OAuth credential disallowed when _rpc_api_keys_only
stakeholders: End user / employee (logs in with an external Google/Azure/Okta/Odoo.com identity)
Portal / public user (self-onboards via 'Sign up with' SSO when signup is allowed)
Security administrator / system admin (registers OAuth providers, supplies client_id, enables/disables IdPs)
External identity provider (Google, Microsoft/Azure AD, Facebook, Okta, Odoo.com — the trusted token issuer)
Module developer (overrides _auth_oauth_signin / _generate_signup_values for custom federation rules)
metrics: count of enabled auth.oauth.provider records (federation breadth)
count of res.users with oauth_provider_id set (SSO adoption / federated-account coverage)
oauth_error redirects (1/2/3) on the login page (SSO failure / denied-access signal)

classification.rationale: auth_oauth is IT identity-and-access infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It owns no business object of its own: its single real model auth.oauth.provider is pure configuration (per-IdP endpoints/client_id/scope), and everything else is an extension of res.users (oauth_uid/token), res.config.settings and ir.config_parameter. It exists solely to let users authenticate to Odoo with an EXTERNAL identity provider (Google, Microsoft/Azure AD, Facebook, Okta, Odoo.com) via the OAuth2 implicit flow, sitting beneath the web login that every other module relies on. It creates no document chain, holds no customer/order/product/ledger data, and produces no primary-activity output, so it is 'support' rather than chain/shop/network. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the precise fit: this is the 'identity & access management' / 'external system integration' capability — a concrete running access-control runtime (OAuth2 callback controller, server-to-server token validation against the IdP, external-to-local identity mapping, JIT provisioning, federated-session token binding). 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance and Resiliency' was considered because SSO touches account-security governance, but rejected: 11.0 is the governance layer (control frameworks, audits, policy management), whereas auth_oauth is the technical implementation IT builds and operates — APQC places that under 8.0 (Develop and manage IT security / identity & access management). The classification mirrors the sibling auth_totp / web records (all 8.0 / support).

standard_capabilities: OAuth2 implicit-flow single-sign-on wired into the standard web/auth_signup login page ('Sign in with X' buttons)

Configurable OAuth2 providers (auth_oauth.provider: auth/validation/data endpoints, client_id, scope, login-button label, CSS) with three seed providers (Odoo.com, Google, Facebook), none enabled by default
Server-to-server access-token validation against the provider UserInfo/tokeninfo endpoint (Bearer header or access_token param)
Subject-key unification across IdPs (sub / id / user_id) with a unique(provider, oauth_uid) local-identity mapping
Just-in-time account provisioning on first SSO login via auth_signup (login/email/name from the validated profile)
/auth_oauth/oea Odoo.com Account login shortcut (no user creation)
OAuth token bound into the session-token fields so token removal/rotation revokes the federated session; one-click Google enablement from Settings
typical_fits: Letting employees log in with corporate Google Workspace identities out of the box (enable provider_google + client_id)
Adding Microsoft/Azure AD (Entra ID), Okta or any OIDC-compliant IdP by creating an auth.oauth.provider record with its endpoints/client_id/scope
Self-service onboarding of portal/customer users via 'Sign up with Google' when auth_signup signup is enabled
Centralizing account-revocation through the external IdP while Odoo trusts the validated token
common_gaps: Implicit 'token' flow only (token in URL fragment); no out-of-box Authorization-Code-with-PKCE flow — modern IdPs may require an add-on/customization
Audience (aud) / Confused-Deputy check against our client_id is intentionally NOT enforced (flagged as a TODO comment) — needs override for strict OIDC validation
No automatic group/role mapping from IdP claims to Odoo groups, and no SCIM-style de-provisioning (deleting at the IdP does not deactivate the Odoo user)
No SAML (separate add-on) and no built-in refresh-token handling — the stored access token is a session credential, not a renewable grant
Provider setup (registering the redirect_uri {base}/auth_oauth/signin at each IdP, client_id) is manual config, not guided per-IdP wizards beyond Google
drive_hints: odoo shell: env.ref('auth_oauth.provider_google').write({'enabled': True, 'client_id': 'XXXX.apps.googleusercontent.com'})  # enable Google SSO
curl -i 'http://localhost:8069/web/login'  # the rendered login page now carries the 'Sign in with ...' provider buttons
curl -i 'http://localhost:8069/auth_oauth/signin?state=%7B%7D'  # without a valid state/token it redirects to /web/login?oauth_error=... (proves the gate)

open_questions: Real provider adoption (which IdPs are enabled, count of federated users) requires runtime data — extract_runtime not run; models empty at capture.
Interplay with sibling auth modules (auth_signup signup modes/invitation tokens, OAuth provider add-ons, SAML) is referenced but lives in other modules — not fully traced.
The auth_oauth.authorization_header ICP (Bearer-header vs query-param token transport) and per-IdP quirks (Facebook data_endpoint) are provider-specific and not exhaustively mapped.
